findings.severity: high (reduce to a cross-reference defect if bytes 55000+ define the mechanism)
findings.artifact: S6 Interaction and race handling; S8 wide layout table; S9 Approval detail; S14 Logging tab
findings.evidence: S6: 'Do not let a tool result, deep link or notification action approve a request by itself.' | S8: '| input.tap | [Deny]  Ask  Allow | Device wide input | ADB connected |' | S9: 'Ask the owner to unlock or authenticate locally for sensitive approvals if the chosen security profile requires it.' | S14: 'RemoteControl and ADB input must not trigger these controls.'
findings.issue: The approval-integrity rules enumerate tool results, deep links and notification actions but not input synthesized by the bridge's own backends. The design gives agents device-wide ADB taps (input.tap) and an ARC Compose input adapter, so an agent can open the approval notification and tap 'Allow once' on the Approvals screen. S14 states the requirement with no mechanism; S6 and S9 do not reference one; the only local-authentication defence is conditional on an undefined 'security profile'. This is a concrete unspecified mechanism for req 5 'No local UI/API/ARC self-approval bypass'.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Add to S6: (a) the admission coordinator refuses to admit any ADB/ARC input-injecting binding while a protected owner surface (Approvals, Clients/pairing, Logging export, Settings) is resumed, and protected surfaces reject Allow while a bridge-originated injection is in flight; (b) the management UI is never an ARC target, or protected surfaces are excluded from any ARC target adapter; (c) replace 'if the chosen security profile requires it' with a concrete rule (e.g. BiometricPrompt BIOMETRIC_STRONG, not device-credential PIN entry, for tools at or above a named risk_class); (d) cross-reference the S15-18 input-provenance mechanism.
findings.verification_needed: Inspect bytes 55000+ (Sections 15-18) for an input-provenance or anti-self-approval mechanism and for a 'security profile' definition. I cannot verify here whether Android exposes a reliable public signal distinguishing shell-injected touch from physical touch; the design must not rely on such a signal without cited evidence.

findings.artifact: S1 opening paragraph; S3 Endpoint protections
findings.evidence: S1: 'exposes generated and schema-driven tools to on-device agents through authenticated loopback Streamable HTTP' | S3: 'Never 0.0.0.0, public interfaces or automatic remote tunneling. Validate Host against the bound endpoint; reject unexpected Origin values and all browser origins by default.'
findings.issue: Req 3 requires a remote-host mode where a PC-side client reaches the device listener through ADB loopback forwarding. Such a connection arrives on device loopback but carries the remote host's Host header (for example 127.0.0.1:<remote port>), which fails an exact match against the bound endpoint whenever ports differ. S1-S3 never acknowledge forwarded remote-host clients, and 'automatic remote tunneling' can be read as excluding the mode.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: In S3 change the Host rule to: accept a Host whose host part is a loopback literal (127.0.0.1, [::1]) or 'localhost' with any port, reject all others (sufficient against DNS rebinding); add: 'Connections arriving through owner-configured adb forward from a remote host are ordinary loopback clients under identical authentication; the bridge never initiates tunnels.'
findings.verification_needed: Check whether the ADB section beyond byte 55000 already defines forwarded-client Host/Origin handling; test whether adbd connects to the device port over IPv4 or IPv6 loopback, which interacts with 'only if tested, ::1'.

findings.artifact: S5 pseudocode; S10 tools and client_tool_rules rows; S12 opening paragraph
findings.evidence: S5: 'require a schema-bound binding rule for EVERY binding; absence or stale hash denies' | S10: 'binding_id and entry_id are the same SHA-256 canonical source-signature identity defined in catalog/README.md'; 'tools / PK tool_id | ... binding associations through tool_binding_aliases'; 'client_tool_rules / PK client_id, tool_id | ... tool_schema_version; effect CHECK deny/ask/allow' | S12: 'Hand-written wrappers are optional ergonomic layers, not the inventory authority.'
findings.issue: Policy is specified per canonical binding with an exact schema hash, but the persisted rule table is keyed by tool_id with a 'tool_schema_version' and no hash; no table in the slice carries binding_id; tool_binding_aliases is referenced but never defined; whether a convenience wrapper's rule suffices or its underlying platform bindings are also evaluated is unspecified. As written the schema cannot represent the evaluator's rule requirement.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define tool_binding_aliases (tool_id FK tools RESTRICT, binding_id TEXT, kind, UNIQUE(binding_id, tool_id)) or state tool_id == binding_id for generated bindings; add schema_hash BLOB to tools and client_tool_rules and state the evaluator compares hashes; add one sentence stating wrappers are canonical tools whose rule is the sole client gate while adapter code enforces wrapper scope.
findings.verification_needed: Catalog/registry sections after byte 55000 and catalog/README.md may define these tables and the identity rule.

findings.artifact: S5 Why capability inventory is separate; S6 Approval binding
findings.evidence: S5: 'A permission callback or UI resume triggers refresh, but stale snapshots cannot guarantee a call will succeed.' | S6: approvalBinding includes 'capabilityGeneration'; 'A changed resource version, target identity, policy revision or capability generation invalidates the approval and requires reevaluation.'
findings.issue: capabilityGeneration semantics are unspecified. If it increments on every refresh, the activity resume the owner performs to reach the Approvals screen invalidates the approval they came to grant, making Ask unusable in the notification path.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define capabilityGeneration as a per-capability_key version incremented only when an observed capability state for that key changes; a refresh with unchanged observations must not increment it; include only the plan's capability keys in the approval binding.

findings.artifact: S4 Manual pairing flow
findings.evidence: 'The agent proves possession of the bootstrap secret and presents a proposed label.'; 'Return it once over the authenticated pairing channel.'; 'Use an explicit pairing surface outside the MCP method catalog and enabled only during a local pairing window.'; 'Manual preconfigured bearer authentication is an interoperability profile'
findings.issue: Steps 2-3 require the agent to run a non-MCP exchange and store a returned secret. Standard MCP clients only support a static URL plus headers, so they cannot complete this flow. The 'manual preconfigured bearer' profile the design relies on for interoperability is never described as a flow, and the pairing surface's path, request/response contract, transport profile and error behaviour are unspecified.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Split S4 into two explicit profiles: (a) Manual: owner mints a credential in Clients, the UI shows credential_id.secret once, owner pastes it into the client configuration, no agent exchange; (b) Bootstrap exchange for cooperating agents: endpoint path, Authorization: Bearer <bootstrap secret> presentation, JSON request/response schema, single-use response, 2-minute expiry and error codes.
findings.verification_needed: Check whether a later section or the C4 dynamic views define the pairing endpoint contract.

findings.artifact: Service boot recovery and status indicators, Optional boot start
findings.evidence: 'A manifest boot receiver reads only a minimal nonsecret boot preference, then requests eligible service startup'; 'Prefer full startup after user unlock, when credential-encrypted SQLite and Keystore material are available.'; 'Persist a small boot preference mirror only, reconcile it with the authoritative configuration after unlock'; 'A blocked or pre-unlock start is reported as Waiting for unlock or Start requires owner action.'
findings.issue: The broadcast(s) handled (BOOT_COMPLETED vs LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED) and the directBootAware status of receiver and service are unspecified. A device-protected preference mirror and a 'Waiting for unlock' status only exist for a direct-boot-aware pre-unlock start, while 'full startup after user unlock' implies a plain BOOT_COMPLETED receiver that could read credential-encrypted storage directly. The two readings require different manifests and state machines.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: State one of: (a) receiver and service are directBootAware, LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED starts the foreground service in 'Waiting for unlock' with no CE access and ACTION_USER_UNLOCKED triggers full start; or (b) only BOOT_COMPLETED is handled post-unlock, drop the mirror and the pre-unlock state.
findings.verification_needed: S19 acceptance evidence (beyond slice) should include the chosen path.

findings.artifact: AppBar and Android status icon; Optional boot start; Independent server and backend health; S11 Migrations
findings.evidence: 'Derive both from actual listener readiness: Starting, Running, Stopping, Stopped or Error.'; 'reported as Waiting for unlock or Start requires owner action'; 'Remain paused or in an explicit error state with owner remediation.'; 'Pause the listener for migrations'
findings.issue: Three states used elsewhere (Waiting for unlock, Start requires owner action, Paused/migrating) are not in the enumerated status set that drives the AppBar and notification.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Publish one status enum covering all states with their AppBar/notification rendering and their interaction with desired_state.

findings.artifact: S2 Baseline and release gates, SQLite row
findings.evidence: 'SQLite native load | Use service-owned Android SQLite access with prepared statements and executable DDL. Prove constraints, triggers, migrations, transactions and catalog scale on every supported Android/ABI profile. [S2]'
findings.issue: The gate name and 'ABI profile' imply a bundled native SQLite, but the content uses platform SQLite whose feature set varies by Android release, not ABI; 'triggers' must be proven yet S10-S11 define none; whether an optional encrypted provider changes the engine is left open.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Rename the gate 'SQLite engine and version floor'; state platform SQLite vs bundled library and the minimum SQLite version per supported Android release; remove 'triggers' or define them in S10.

findings.artifact: S2 Baseline; Optional boot start; AppBar and Android status icon
findings.evidence: 'Select minimum Android API and supported devices from product needs and current support tiers, not from a generic old template. [S1]'; 'Android 15 limits BOOT_COMPLETED starts for several service types'; 'On Android 13+, denial can suppress'

findings.artifact: S10 credentials row; S4
findings.evidence: 'kind CHECK mcp/admin'; 'Do not expose admin methods, policy mutation or token creation as agent tools.'
findings.issue: An 'admin' credential kind is persisted but no admin credential consumer or surface is defined in the slice.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define the admin credential's consumer (for example the package-aware pairing entry point or export/import) or remove the value.

findings.artifact: S10 executions row; Independent server and backend health; S11 Permission commit and execution admission; S6 state table; S4 Rotate row
findings.evidence: 'state CHECK admitted/dispatched/completed/failed/canceled/unknown'; 'admitted operations become interrupted or unknown and are never replayed'; 'reserve/consume an in memory one use approval ... a reserved approval is invalidated rather than restored optimistically'; approval states Pending/Approved/Consumed/Terminal; 'At its end, atomically revoke old, increment client epoch and move retained replacement to that epoch.' with clients.credential_epoch and credentials.epoch both defined
findings.issue: 'interrupted' is not a permitted execution state; 'reserved' is not an approval state; which epoch (clients.credential_epoch or credentials.epoch) sessions bind to during rotation overlap is implicit.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Map interrupted to unknown (or add it to CHECK); add Reserved between Approved and Consumed with 'commit failure returns to invalidated'; state sessions bind to clients.credential_epoch and the replacement credential carries the current epoch during overlap.

findings.artifact: S11 Indexes and connection policy; S10 closing paragraph
findings.evidence: 'Add a partial unique index on executions(client_id, tool_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL. Generate keys per intended operation, not per HTTP retry; reject reuse with a different request digest.'; 'ordinary call arguments/results stay in memory and die on restart.'
findings.issue: MCP tools/call has no idempotency field, so the carrier is unspecified; the response to a duplicate key with the same digest is unspecified and cannot replay results because results are not persisted.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Declare idempotency_key as an optional adapter-schema argument for write tools; duplicate with same digest returns the recorded execution state under a DUPLICATE_OPERATION code with no result replay; duplicate with different digest returns a defined error code.

findings.artifact: S3 One tool call step 1-2; S12 Error contract; Independent server and backend health
findings.evidence: 'Reject unknown fields, invalid types and out of range values.'; 'Use protocol errors for malformed or unsupported JSON-RPC/MCP requests; use a tool result with isError for a valid call that cannot execute'; 'Validate session ownership and negotiated protocol.'; 'Old sessions and approvals expire'
findings.issue: Whether argument-schema violations are JSON-RPC -32602 or isError results is not stated; handling of a missing MCP-Protocol-Version header, an unsupported version, and an unknown or boot-expired session is not stated in HTTP terms.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: State: schema violations produce JSON-RPC -32602; missing header follows the specification default then is rejected if incompatible with the negotiated session; unsupported version produces HTTP 400; unknown or boot-expired session produces HTTP 404 so clients re-initialize.
findings.verification_needed: Against the supplied 2025-11-25 transports and tools pages.

findings.artifact: S3 opening paragraph; S3 Discovery and streams
findings.evidence: 'Implement its initialization, protocol version negotiation, POST handling and optional GET SSE behavior as a coherent profile.'; 'Send negotiated list-change notifications after registry changes.'
findings.issue: list_changed and resources/updated notifications need a server-to-client channel; calling GET SSE 'optional' leaves delivery undefined when no POST stream is open.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: State that the bridge implements GET SSE (optional only in the specification's sense), returns 405 only when disabled by owner configuration, and queues notifications per session with bounded drop-oldest semantics while no stream is open.

findings.artifact: S3 Endpoint protections; S7 Connection reconnects row
findings.evidence: 'Bind sessions and event cursors to client, credential epoch and server boot identifier.'; 'Default v1 has no durable transport SSE replay; separately retained callback journals are read through resources/read'
findings.issue: 'Event cursors' is ambiguous. Binding to the boot identifier is correct for transport SSE event IDs but would break post-restart reads of the durable callback journal if it means application cursors; whether SSE event IDs are emitted at all in v1 is unstated.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Replace 'event cursors' with 'SSE event IDs', state whether they are emitted in v1, and state that journal cursors bind to client and journal identity, not boot ID.

findings.artifact: S5 opening paragraph and pseudocode
findings.evidence: 'A required entry-point tool rule can only restrict binding authority.'; 'unknown raw calls require an explicit broad raw backend/service grant and tool rule'; 'No wildcard tools, rule priorities, inherited Allow or regular expression permission language.'
findings.issue: 'Entry-point tool' is never defined; the 'broad raw backend/service grant' has no schema representation and reads as a wildcard unless modelled as an exact scope set.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define entry-point tools as the enumerated generic tools (binding.invoke, the raw Binder tool, dynamic aliases) and model the raw grant as the raw tool rule's scope_json exact set of service identities and transaction-code ranges.

findings.artifact: S10 change_outbox row; S11 bridge_config row
findings.evidence: 'change_outbox / PK change_id | ... Written in the same transaction as policy changes; delivery is idempotent.'; bridge_config includes 'fgs_type'

findings.artifact: S6 Approval binding and Interaction; S7 Connection reconnects row
findings.evidence: 'Socket disconnection alone is not MCP cancellation; the original deadline still applies. [S4]'; 'Proposed approval lifetime is 60 seconds, capped by the caller deadline.'; 'Default v1 has no durable transport SSE replay'
findings.issue: If the POST stream closes after admission, the effect executes but the final JSON-RPC response has no delivery path; the outcome is not stated. 'Caller deadline' has no MCP carrier and is undefined.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: State: after admission the result is recorded in executions/audit only and discarded, never replayed; define 'caller deadline' as the server's bounded transport time for the request (no client field) and the resulting APPROVAL_EXPIRED behaviour.

findings.artifact: S8 wide layout table; S9 Approval detail
findings.evidence: 'fingerprint 6F2A'; 'Show stable client fingerprint and selected resource summary.'
findings.issue: Fingerprint derivation and length are unspecified; the 16-bit example is collision-prone across clients and can be confused in approval dialogs.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Define the fingerprint as the first 8 or more hex characters of SHA-256(credential_id), full value on detail screens, and state wireframe values are illustrative.

findings.area: concurrency of optional logging vs admission (req 2)
findings.artifact: S11 Indexes and connection policy; S14 SQLite extension
findings.evidence: 'short transactions and a single application writer queue'; 'Enforce each client quota and the global budget in the writer transaction'
findings.issue: Whether optional call-log writes run under the admission gate is unspecified; a diagnostic flood could delay admissions.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: State optional log writes are outside the admission gate, batched through the writer queue, and dropped with a counter when the queue is saturated.

verified_resolutions: Brightness: S12 states documented range 1..255 with a narrower default policy range 16..240; consistent with the supplied official fact and with the S8 wireframe rows.
All-Kotlin: S2 'Both the MCP server and management UI are Kotlin' and 'No .NET runtime is required by the bridge' satisfy req 2 supersession of the Avalonia/.NET UI.

Persistent service: S7 requires a foreground service independent of the activity, START_STICKY with null-Intent handling, stopWithTask disabled, desired_state persisted separately from observed health, and honest OS-blocked start states; req 2.

Separate health: 'The MCP server remains running even when self-ADB needs re-pairing or a target is offline' and 'ADB offline adds a separate backend warning while the MCP Running icon remains'; req 2 (device-view health deferred to later sections).
Deny by default and OS-unavailable as observed state, not policy: Design commitments and S5 check table; discovery never grants; req 5.
Admission as linearization point with gate, snapshot install before acknowledgement, dispatch outside the SQLite transaction, no lock held during human wait or Binder work: S7, S11, S6.

MCP 2025-11-25 pinned as a deliberate baseline; example headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Session-Id, Accept with both media types) match the specification; disconnection is not cancellation; no invented approval polling method; progress only when negotiated; req 9.
Per-client logging in SQLite with Off/Metadata/Redacted modes, separate logging_revision, bounded quotas and reserved audit budget: S14; req 2.
Secrets: HMAC-SHA-256 verifier under a non-exportable Keystore key, no raw tokens or HMAC key in SQLite, honest statement that a compromised process can still invoke keys: S11.

Honest limits stated rather than hidden: same-process facade is not a privilege boundary; plain-HTTP port impersonation residual risk; allowBackup=false is not a universal transfer guarantee; Android 13+ notification denial behaviour.

No tools were used; the sha256, cited sources, Structurizr, Gradle and SVG artifacts were not inspected; the prior design013 ledger was not available in this pass, so no regression comparison was made.

Platform uncertainties reported as uncertainty, not fact: whether Android exposes a public signal distinguishing shell-injected touch from physical touch; whether the chosen Ktor engine supports TLS with an Android Keystore-held server key; whether writing the integer SCREEN_BRIGHTNESS setting reads back exactly on recent Android releases, which affects S12 'conflict' detection; whether exported=false receivers reliably receive BOOT_COMPLETED on all supported releases.
Requirements 4, 6, 10 and 11 are not materially present in this byte range and were not scored; absence here is not a defect.
